g.text: Down Home Creole · Phase 1 · P1-304 Drum-top vibratory sifter (built in house) · rev B
UNLESS NOTED: LINEAR ±0.5 [±.02] · HOLES +0.2/-0 · ANGLES ±0.5° · MACHINED X.X ±0.1, X.XX ±0.05 · THIRD-ANGLE PROJECTION · BREAK EDGES 0.5 · ASME Y14.5

svg.text: 1 Base on the drum rim, 3 isolators
3 Flex band across the 4 mm gap
orange = parts added in that step; ghosted = parts still to come
base sits flat on the rim, no rock; tabs clear the rim 1.5
H3 x4 M10, 45 N·m + thread lock
weights equal top and bottom; paint-mark the setting
gap body to upstand 4 ±1 all round; body level ±1 mm
band not tight: 10 slack, no contact with the drum
H5 x2 M8, 12 N·m, serrated washers
magnet sits on both bars, no rock
deck drops in by hand, ≤ 1 radial play
3 pads touch the deck (2 squeeze); lid does not rattle
sock slack, does not pull the lid
1. Bench: screw the 3 isolators P1-341 into the seat ring P1-304-101 (lower stud through the Ø9 hole, nut H1 underneath). Base on a clean drum: tabs outside the rim, skirt inside the liner.
2. Bench: vibrator P1-306 on bracket P1-304-206, motor axis vertical, terminal box down; set both eccentric weights to the ITP setting (start 80 %).
3. Lift the body with the vibrator (≈ 23 kg [51 lb], 2 people) onto the isolator studs through the bracket holes.
4. Flex band P1-344 over the upstand and the body bottom, 2 worm clamps; leave the slack loop outward.
5. Bond strap P1-347 from the seat-ring hole (60°, R330) to the isolator bracket at 90°.
6. Grate magnet P1-307 on the 2 bars, tubes across the flow.
7. Deck gasket P1-304-502 on the ledge, then the screen deck P1-304-400, cloth up.
8. Lid P1-304-300 with gasket P1-304-501; close the 4 draw latches P1-342 crosswise.
9. Sock P1-346 from the blender valve to the 4 in inlet ferrule; dust port kit P1-345 and the collector hose on the 3 in ferrule.
10. Cord P1-350 from the isolator Q-306 to the vibrator box with a drip loop, tied to the bracket; wire per E01/E02.
11. Commission per P1-304-900 (rotation not relevant, amplitude, current, interlock with the valve).
OPERATION, SCREEN CHECK, CLEANING (about 10 min per changeover)

1. Drum change (every batch): vibrator OFF on the HMI and the valve closed. Unlatch nothing: 2 people lift the whole sifter (≈ 48 kg [106 lb]) by the seat ring, outside the isolators, and set it on the next drum; or slide the drums on the dolly if the
2. Before lifting: the cord P1-350 has 3 m and a drip loop; the sock and the dust hose come off at their TC clamps first.

3. Screen change / check (every batch end, ITP T19): lock out Q-306; open the 4 latches; lift the lid; lift out the deck; inspect the cloth for tears; lift out the magnet; wipe the tubes into a bag (record the catch); refit.

4. Allergen changeover: lock out; lid, deck, magnet, gaskets to the sink (warm detergent, rinse, sanitise, air dry). Body: vacuum then wipe inside, band off and washed. Base skirt wiped. ATP swab the deck and shell (T23).
5. Never wash the vibrator with a jet; it is IP66 but the cord grip is the weak point. Never strike the cloth to clear it: use a soft brush from below.
6. Spare deck P1-304-400 (make 2) is kept clean and bagged so a torn screen costs one lid opening, not a batch.
Hex nut M8 nyloc A2 + flat washer (isolator lower stud)
Hex nut M8 nyloc A2 + flat washer (isolator upper stud)
